text:
Standards and World Trade: WTO and TBT Agreement 
1. Why Do Trade Rules Affect Technical Standards? International trade is affected not only by tariffs, but also by technical requirements. Tariff 
A tariff is a tax/duty on imported goods. 
• 
It is visible and measurable. 
• 
Governments negotiate tariff rates openly.
creator: Microsoft® Word 2024
author: nitiny2k17@gmail.com

text:
Tariff 
A tariff is a tax/duty on imported goods. 
• 
It is visible and measurable. 
• 
Governments negotiate tariff rates openly. Technical Regulations 
A country may introduce technical requirements such as: 
• 
Safety rules 
• 
Labelling requirements 
• 
Testing procedures 
• 
Product requirements 
These rules may be created for genuine reasons such as safety or quality, but they can 
also make foreign products more difficult or expensive to sell. Therefore, technical regulations can sometimes act as non-tariff barriers to trade.

2. Why Was the TBT Agreement Created? TBT = Technical Barriers to Trade 
After 1947, GATT negotiations gradually reduced tariffs.

TBT = Technical Barriers to Trade 
After 1947, GATT negotiations gradually reduced tariffs. As tariffs became lower, the importance of non-tariff barriers increased.

As tariffs became lower, the importance of non-tariff barriers increased. Technical regulations could be used: 
• 
For legitimate purposes such as safety and health

Or as a disguised barrier against foreign products 
Therefore, the WTO created rules to ensure that technical regulations do not create 
unnecessary obstacles to international trade.

TBT (Technical Barriers to Trade) Agreement is a set of international rules that ensures 
technical regulations, product standards, and testing procedures do not create 
unnecessary obstacles to global trade.

TBT Agreement – Definition 
TBT (Technical Barriers to Trade) Agreement is a set of international rules that ensures 
technical regulations, product standards, and testing procedures do not create 
unnecessary obstacles to global trade. In simple words: 
Countries can make technical rules, but those rules should not unnecessarily 
restrict international trade.
